Origins

Flemings - an ancient genus of the northern coast, once owned the entire coast of the Ice Sea. (Sea of Ice) His father told young Benedict that the Flemings had revolted three times against the Origins, twice defeated them in great battles, and once took the First Winter by storm. According to the legend of the Sword of the Voice of Winter, the Counts of Fleming deceived the stronghold; Duke Lioreus Origin surrendered only when the Count threatened to kill all the inhabitants of the castle, and was buried alive with the sword, and his heir later cut off the treacherous Fleming’s head. Iona told a similar story differently: the Earl of Godfrey Fleming took the First Winter and killed the Duke of Odar Origin, for which the Origins executed the Count with all their near relatives, and the Fleming family was revived from the bastards. How these two stories relate, none of the narrators explain.

Lady Karen, in the collector's edition of Arrow, Coin, Spark, writes that Duke Liorei Origin surrendered to the rebellious Flemings to save the lives of his subjects, and ended his days in the First Winter's dungeon. (Arrow, Coin, Spark (Collector's Edition)) But the rebellion cost the rebels dearly: their clan was almost destroyed, and Fleming's house was revived from the bastards.

Benedict's great-grandfather, Lord Goram Fleming, went three times against the pirates of the Sunset Coast who settled on the Seal Islands. The present Earl's grandfather kneeled before the Origins. Benedict himself served the Duke of Desmond for twenty-two years and participated in four of his wars. His fleet deployed northern troops in the Shayland War, and in 1760 and 1764 he successfully fought in the Gran Islands archipelago.

Appearance and Faith

Benedict is a huge broad-shouldered man, like a blacksmith, with a curly beard, a big forehead and blue eyes; in the Shadow of the Great Tree, his beard is called black. He is a "good man" and an orthodox fanatical admirer of Gloria the Intercessor. Visiting the temples of his mother, in the question of women, he held his paternal views: a man in a family is “a god and a judge.” His advisor and ambassador is the vain gray-haired Abbot Hosh. Fleming likes to talk about his ancestors, and reads rarely and with difficulty.

In Arrow, Coin, Spark and Only One Star

Old ties with the Origins

The Flemings visited the first winter. The Count held little Iona on his knees, and young Erwin once climbed with one of Fleming's daughters into a tower with singing pipes; the girl pleased him because he knew the word "perspective". Lady Sophia later regretted that her son was not married to Molly Fleming: "less would be sad - and with Flemings, and with you." When in August 1774 Erwin returned from the Outback to his father, who was broken by illness, Sophia anxiously told her son that the First Winter was empty, and that the Earl of Fleming and Baron White, who were related to the Origins, could rebel: White was collecting banners in the Belomorye, Fleming had gone west with the ships, and Fleming had already twice managed to take the First.

Delay

When Erwin rebelled and summoned the vassals, Fleming and Baron White, who owned three-quarters of the Duke's fleet, detained their battalions. They held joint exercises in the Valley of the Blind Virgins and did not want to participate in the “madness”. In September 1774, the mountain guard reported to Erwin that three battalions of White and Fleming were camped in the valley and were not moving. The loss of these lords of the northern ports, to which three-quarters of the fleet and about a thousand kairs were subject, would deprive Erwin of the seventh part of the army. Deciding that since they are not strengthening and do not go home, it means that they are hesitating, Erwin sent a message to the valley: "My Lord Fleming, forty-two hours" - and placed a mountain guard in the mountains between the valley and the Southern Way in case the vassals crossed. In the end, Fleming reasoned that the betrayal was against the gods and that Origin easily banned them in that valley. He literally grabbed White by the beard and brought him to the First Winter, where the baron was in prison. Mark believed that the count's hesitation ended when Adrian burned Evergard with the Rings: such sacrilege the pious count could not stand.

Erwin forgave the delay on one condition: the count had to sail to the Beyond and bring the Talking Objects from there. To Jemis, appointed as guide and adviser to the expedition, Erwin announced that the count had "proved his loyalty in the Valley of the Blind Virgins" and would go with three hundred warriors; later, Erwin confessed to Alanis that he did not trust only two of all vassals - Fleming and White - and therefore "now one in the Beyond, and the second in prison." Among the sailors of the flotilla there were rumors that the count had gathered the captains for a secret council and that the expedition was punitive; Mark, listening to them, figured out on whose side the cairns loyal at the same time to Fleming and Origin, if the count again "salts" against the Duke. Fleming considered the order humiliating, because instead of commanding the northern army, he was sent to the “unglorious Beyond”. With his flotilla went Jemis Lilliday and secretly Mark.

Anonymous letter and “sign”

Even before sailing on the deck of the flagship "White Star" was planted with an anonymous letter: the war of Origin is lost, the count is given an honest opportunity to leave "from the dying ship", and in confirmation in the Beyond he will be shown the Sign. On the way, Fleming asked Mark what people behind the River believed. Under threat of reprisal, Mark composed that Adrian's true power was faith and that he was the messenger of the gods. Fleming forbade exploration (according to the guess of Jemis, so that no one could get to the Persians before the count) and publicly reprimanded Jemis for volunteering to go to the fort.

Behind the River before their eyes disappeared fort heretics: in its place remained a round funnel. Fleming fell to his knees and considered it a sign of Gloria. He decided that Adrian was the vicegerent of the gods, and Origin was cursed. As it turned out later, the secret order had its agent surrounded by the count: he told the order about the disappearance of the fort.

Treason

Fleming summoned Mark to his cabin and announced that he would take the First Winter, and the heads of Lord Desmond and Lady Sophia would send Adrian. Mark had to go to the emperor as a mediator. The men of the earl were ordered to kill on the ship "The Seal" all who would remain faithful to Origin. Mark struck the count with a spark from the Item given by Jemis, and fled through the window of the stern. “He was crumbling like a kitchen cabinet,” Crow later said. Of the entire fleet, only the crew of the Seal remained faithful to the Origins.

In the Interlude, "Speaking to God", Fleming's three ships chase the Seal off the coast, and the count's riders chase the survivors in the mountains of Origin to the bridge over the Valley of the Gods. (He Who Speaks with God)

In "A Doll on the Throne" and "Yanmei Hunt"

Failure

Fleming deployed a squadron and left for the Belomorye. The plan was simple: to suddenly capture the almost empty First Winter, swear an oath to Adrian, and receive the entire duchy as a reward. However, a sudden attack failed: one ship fought off the squadron, and his team alerted the Duke's warriors. The count gathered all the troops from the coast, attracted the relatives of the prisoner White, took some of the commands from the ships and scored fifteen hundred swords. He was with them for the first winter when the news of Adrian's death came. The Earl prayed for Minerva to throw spark troops at Origin, but the Lords recognized Erwin's power, and Fleming's dream was to preserve the Belomorye. Against him stood the Duke's army of twenty thousand; the delay was only given by the distance: from Faunterra to the Belomorye two months of march. Rumors of the mutiny reached the Southern Way: on the advice of the Duke of Labelin in the winter of 1775, the Marquis of Windley offered to join with the Earl of Fleming, who "with five hundred cairns" keeps the coast of the Ice Sea, and together go to the First Winter. Due to the mutiny, the sea route to Origin became dangerous, and Waymar stopped bringing northern mail pigeons. In the spring, Desmond advised his son to withdraw the battalions from Faunterra and throw them to hold the Southern Way and suppress Fleming's rebellion. The “Voice of the Crown” deliberately mentioned this far-off rebellion so that the newspaper did not look like propaganda.

Erwin saw Fleming as a possible Puppet Master, but rejected this idea: Fleming is a fanatic, and the Puppet Master is not. Erwin even suspected that the treasonous idea was planted by Count Mark, who spoke to him in private. He explained to his sister that the “stupid rebellion” would resolve itself: after the fall of the tyrant, Fleming could not harm.

Negotiations through Vittor

In April 1775, Vittor Shayland offered to become an intermediary in exchange for the right of duty-free trade through the Belomorye and the opening of banking offices on the coast of the Sea of Ice. Fleming sent Abbot Hoch to Waymar. Iona reluctantly accepted the abbot, recalling that the count had once given her a horse for her tenth birthday, and then wanted to capture the castle where her mother lived. The abbot offered to give the marriage of Violet at the discretion of Erwin and pay tribute, first thirty, then fifty thousand ephes. Iona rejected the one-time payment as a bribe and demanded that the Origins take under their command the free captains of the northern fleet with the right to collect tax from them. In addition, the count had to personally apologize to Erwin; the traditional form of atonement she called self-flagellation with salt lash and the cutting off of two fingers. Vittor proposed Waymar as the meeting place and allowed the earl to bring a battalion of kairs there through Shayland's lands. Iona found it strange, but did not argue.

In "Humans and Gods"

Fleming's Belomorye battalion entered Torrey from the Sea of Ice; burlaps and oxen dragged his ships against the stream to Waymar. Vittor sent a letter to Count Martin and Joaquin. Martin told Fleming about the "miracle of the resurrection" of Vittor, and the count, outraged that the believers had not yet known anything, recognized him as "the Chosen One." When Desmond's squadron fired at his ships, Fleming shouted "With us is the power of the gods!" and led the men ashore. In the river port (the battle is told later, in the "Shadow of the Great Tree"), the White Seamen, together with Joaquin, who fired from the Perst, met twice as many kairs of the First Winter. As Joaquin later realized, the destruction of Fleming's battalion was Desmond's true goal in this battle. A regiment of sunsets was coming down to help Fleming, but when they came across the fleeing northerners, the sunsets took them for the cues of the First Winter. In the end, the victory remained for Desmond, and Fleming, like Horis, lost the wagon. (General Oris)

The Shadow of the Great Tree

The Siege of Waymar

In the besieged Shayland Castle, Fleming was part of Vittor's inner circle with Richard and Martin. His severely wounded, rotting in the heat without medicine, he prayed for their souls and finished off with blows of mercy. He despised the truism of the sunsets, referring to the commandment “Let another be”, which, according to him, has a limit. When Desmond poisoned the castle well, and Paul could not swim from behind the calm until five days later, Fleming was the first to understand the meaning of the scarlet flag over the Origin regiments - refusing to negotiate - and confirmed Richard's words that the House Origin cannot be blackmailed by a hostage. He suggested a way out: kill the sunsets with their own hands against honor, but they can be sent into a hopeless attack, where corpse-eaters will “accept a glorious death”, and the rest will have enough water for three days. Vittor picked up on this idea, and Joaquin, who stood up for the allies, Fleming stated that he who ate a dead body and shared a bed with a heretic, needed redemption and that he himself would have done much more to him. When the enemies poisoned the castle well, Vittor called it a "God's test", which he passed along with Fleming and Richard, and the count showed with all his appearance that he was ready to sign under every word. When the Agathans left Waymar, and the army of the Gallard parish approached the castle, the count forgot the contempt for the corpse-eaters and shook hands with Horace. Fleming was among the guests invited to the chapel for the ritual of the Absolute. When Paul's Shavans rushed at Richard, Ice called for Fleming and Joaquin to help, and the count "like a bear" broke into the ranks of the Shavans. After the death of Vittor, Fleming, Ice and Horis were perplexedly revised, not knowing who the commander was now, and when Vittor “resurrected” at the test of the Absolute, Fleming and the abbot knelt after the sunsets. The Count, like General Horis, Lady Laura and Bishop Amessin, sent out pigeons with the news that Vittor had died, returned to life, and the priory killed Alanis; copies of these ribbons lay on Minerva's table.

Hiking in the First Winter

In the army of the Chosen Fleming was the first of the generals to obey Richard with his White Seamen and, knowing the terrain well, supported him on the advice. In September 1775, as Vittor's army was marching through Northwood, Fleming, along with Dorcaster, supported Ice's plan to turn west and be the first to break up Desmond's hasty Craig Northwood, leading to a victory at Fox Dole. (Fox Vale) He also suggested that Vittor impersonate Martin his youngest daughter Violet, addressing the count as if he were completely in control of his brother's fate; Vittor promised to think. Belomorye moved to the side of Kuklovod, and the son of Count Osmund, opening his father's letter, took the second battalion to the First Winter, where he blocked the northern road into the valley. According to Richard, only he and Fleming could lead the army through Gates of Heaven.

Hostages

Erwin cunningly seized the ship of Fleming's son-in-law, Lord Velentyne, and with the help of Molly, who brought a fake invitation from Vittor, lured Lady Agnia with Violetta from the Belomorye (the chapter "Arrow - 9" is told on behalf of Agnia). The Count with a dozen kairs and an abbot came to the meeting in a ruined inn on the pass, nicknamed the "Devil's Hole". Agnia's letter consisted of an apology, and the count read it with apparent approval. Fleming refused to betray the Chosen One: the gods, he said, would like to test whether he could sacrifice his daughters to faith. Erwin conceded: the earl could not fight for Origin, but undertook to withdraw from the battle, stay with his battalion in Gates of Heaven, and lead Osmund's battalion off the northern road. Erwin promised to release the hostage immediately after the battle at any outcome, and in case of his victory, he swore to Agatha to do it on the same day. When asked about his own fate, the count chose an apology instead of a severed head. Erwin believed that in one year the count betrayed him three times.

In late November 1775, as the Chosen One's army was marching towards the First Winter, Fleming personally led the flanking dozers that covered the wagons on the mountain road - a role too small for the count, and General Horis, through Hash Eilish, conveyed to the Chosen One the suspicion that Fleming was looking for a reason to be excommunicated from the army. Soon after, the count approached Vittor, called his speech a new manifestation of holiness, and announced that he should bring repentance. His cuirrs received an order: when meeting with Erwin's detachment, let the duke pass without a fight and report to the count. When Erwin's detachment came across a Belomorye patrol at the Sky Squaws, the captive cyre admitted it, and Erwin realized that this time Fleming had shown "wild loyalty" to the Puppeteer and would set a trap on the northern road, which the Duke himself had named to him.

The ambush on the Belomorye road

Fleming broke his promise. Erwin and Jemis foresaw this: the Duke himself called the count his way, calculating that he would want to capture the detachment and find out where the hostages were hidden, and at the same time to have time for the assault. The ambush was set in a gorge on the Belomorye road, a couple of miles from the First Winter. The court of Adrian, watching the battle across the Bird without the Plot, saw the White Sears occupy the rocks above the road, and decided that the trap had succeeded. However, Gordon Sue's Xs stopped two hundred yards from the wreck, and Commandant and Murdoch's cues, along with Jemis and the Gun, went down the shepherd trail to the rear. (The Weapon) Fire of the White Sears boldly from the ledges. Some of their Xs were driven away towards the Belomorye, the rest were caught; a hundred people, including the count himself, were captured. Nexia Flame, dressed as a shepherdess, passed through Belomorye positions the day before to hand Lord Desmond Erwin's plan, and Violet was sent under guard to a mountain fort. During the battle for the First Winter on the Belomorye road appeared kairs in two-color coats. (Battle for First Winter) The court of Adrian took them for the victorious White Seamen, but they were disguised Xes: standing on the flank of Richard's corps, they raised the Origins and captured Richard himself. The remains of Fleming's keel left in the Belomorye after the battle.

In "Fantasies"

The author calls "Fantasies" fantasies about how the fates of heroes can develop after the main plot.

In 1776, Erwin showed Shavan envoy Neymir a glacier deep under the castle of the First Winter. (Neimir) There lay the naked Count Benedict Fleming, frozen alive and covered with an inch layer of ice.

“You may have heard the expression, ‘Forgiven as Benedict.’

According to Erwin, in this form, the count was taken to the cities of the duchy, so that all vassals would be convinced of the "mercy" of the seigneur, and Fleming's last words were gratitude for kindness. Erwin noticed that there was no wife or daughter next to the count. The Chavanese ambassadors, who sailed to the First Winter, bypassing Polaris, on the way offered condolences to the “recently widowed” Lady Fleming in the Belomorye, where the Origen garrison already stood. In the fantasy of "Ad-ri-an!", Vladyka Adrian, hoping that, left "without a head", the vassals of the First Winter would fight for power, remarked: "It's a pity, Fleming on the Star ... but he has children."

Family

  • Lady Agnia is a wife, obedient and fearful; she did not leave the castle for six months and waited for the decision of the man in everything.
  • Molly is the eldest daughter, the wife of Lord Velentyne from the Gran Islands; helped Erwin to lure out her mother and sister, begged to spare her husband: "The beloved was simply deceived."
  • Violetta is the youngest daughter, the fourth child in the family. In her youth, she was in love with Erwin and kissed him three times; the count did not dare to offer her to Desmond as a daughter-in-law. In captivity, Erwin kept fun and daring.
  • Osmund is the son, commander of the second, Ice Battalion.

According to Karen, Count Benedict, ruler of the Belomorye and half of the northern coast, is one of the strongest lords of the North along with Lilliday, Statham and Main. He has two sons and two daughters. Molly after marriage disappeared from social life; it is said that she is very fat and wears a monstrous amount of powder - allegedly to hide the bruises from the beatings of her husband. Violetta during the events of the first novel and two more years after remained unmarried, lived in the Belomorye, led with her mother the finances of the county, and her father even married her for Martin Shayland. Karen hints that Violette “has a significant role in history,” but did not talk about it.

Jemis Lilliday recalled that in his youth he was married to Molly Fleming, but he ran away on a hike, and when he returned, she was already married, gave birth to a son and became very fat. (In early media outlets, the bride is referred to simply as "Lady Fleming.")

Personality

Fleming is a rude and quick-tempered man, but not a coward: in the Beyond, he drew a sword against Jemis, who held the Ring. He fully relies on “signs”, and under the guise of piety hides self-love and duplicity. Erwin wanted to "slip boiling water into this vile face" for his arguments about the victim's daughters.

Appearances

  • "Arrow, coin, spark" - referred to as a vassal, slow with the troops.
  • "Only One Star" - an expedition to the Beyond, treason (head Mark).
  • "Speaking to God" is the pursuit of the Seal team.
  • A Doll on the Throne, the Yanmei Hunt, is a rebellion in the Belomorye, negotiated through Hosha.
  • "Humans and Gods", "The Shadow of the Great Tree" - on the side of Vittor; captivity.
  • “Fantasies” is a frozen body in a glacier.
